primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Identity-theft / wrong-person expungement under 22 O.S. § 19a and the Section 18 identity-theft category: available where the person was charged, arrested, or subject to a warrant for a crime committed by another person who used their name or identifying information without consent.

Section 18/19 adult expungement under 22 O.S. §§ 18-19 covers categories including acquittal, conviction reversed and dismissed, DNA factual innocence, arrest with no charges filed, all charges dismissed without a deferred judgment, deferred/delayed-sentence dismissals, eligible misdemeanor and felony convictions, a nonviolent felony reclassified as a misdemeanor, full gubernatorial pardons, and identity-theft / wrong-person records.

Section 19 procedure under 22 O.S. § 19: the qualified person petitions the district court where the arrest information is located; the court sets a hearing with 30 days' notice to the prosecuting agency, arresting agency, OSBI, and any other relevant agency, and may seal records if the harm to privacy or danger of unwarranted adverse consequences outweighs the public interest in retaining them. After sealing, the official actions are deemed never to have occurred. Section 19 does not authorize physical destruction of criminal-justice records.

counselFlags: Expungement means sealing: In Oklahoma, expungement usually means the record is sealed from public view. Some categories are fully sealed, but many are only partially sealed, meaning law enforcement can still access them. It does not always mean the record is physically destroyed.
Scope limits: An Oklahoma expungement does not clear federal, tribal, military, or out-of-state records, does not restore firearm rights, and does not fix immigration consequences.

Registry build blocker: the enrolled text of 22 O.S. §§ 18 and 19 as amended by Senate Bill 2030 (2026) was not obtained; the Section 18 category numbering is unstable after three consecutive years of amendments, so the eligibility screen runs on the category description, never a paragraph number.

Registry release blocker: before any paid petition, screen whether the participant is reached by the SB 2030 sealing-without-petition route; generating a paid petition for someone entitled to a free route is the specific harm the controlling review warns against.

Registry release blocker: the district court filing fee is not established and must not be stated to a participant; OSBI states the court-record expungement is free while an arrest-record expungement carries a $150 OSBI processing fee (cashier's check or money order only).

The source records that the participant signs and verifies the petition but establishes no notarization requirement and no specific verification statute; confirm the required verification form with counsel before filing.

Notice is the court's act under 22 O.S. § 19 (hearing set with 30 days' notice to the prosecuting agency, arresting agency, OSBI, and any other relevant agency); the proposed order must identify every agency to which it applies.
One petition per county; multiple arrests in the same county may be combined, separate counties require separate petitions.
Any dispute about whether the participant is the subject of the record, any tribal-court record (a live post-McGirt issue), and any contested hearing end self-help and require attorney review.

Full versus partial sealing changes the outcome and must be disclosed; § 19 does not authorize physical destruction, and a sealed record may be unsealed on changed conditions or destroyed after ten years under § 19(N).
